newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen leader pledges crime fight, talks go on. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Chechen leader pledges crime fight, talks go on. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]

text.p: Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov pledged on Tuesday to fight a wave of kidnapping that has gripped Russia's separatist region and a senior minister went to Moscow to discuss the peace process.
Maskhadov told a news conference in the regional capital Grozny that he planned frequent police and commando raids, after an operation on Monday freed at least six captives.
"Such raids will be carried out quickly and suddenly. The units involved will be on red alert all the time, day and night," Maskhadov said.
Chechen police units on Monday freed an Austrian businessman who had been held hostage in Chechnya and five other captives.
But seven Russian journalists were still being held, some of them after months in captivity.
Maskhadov said he had expected three (corrects from four) reporters from Russia's NTV commercial television to be freed in Monday's raid, but it did not happen.
"I was 100 percent sure on Monday that the NTV journalists would be freed, but there are certain mishaps. I am sure we are following the right trace," Maskhadov said.

The kidnappings have undermined efforts by authorities in the Caucasus region to restore order since a peace deal last August ended 21 months of fighting between pro-independence guerrilla fighters and Russian troops.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Maskhadov signed a peace accord last month promising to end centuries of conflict between Moscow and the Chechens.

Chechen Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov arrived in Moscow, where he was expected to meet Russian officials for talks on economic parts of the peace deal, including a banking agreement, customs policies and oil trasnportation.
